name: playtest_sunset
description: Not a test — the install step for a hands-on session at SUNSET with §25c's RAYMARCH ON, run with --hold. The raymarch now carries §25d's shaping rather than bypassing it: the volume is baked with the same narrowed falloff, the same rim bite that keeps the border ragged instead of circular, the same filled-in thin decks and the same density gamma, because its alpha is this volume's optical depth and it never reads the 2-D atlas. It also has a separate LIGHT extinction (see CloudRaymarchMath.LightExtinctionFor): at the density that makes a 3.4-texel cirrus deck visible from above, a grazing sunset ray stays inside it for ~80 texels and is fully occluded, which rendered the deck that should be last-lit as the darkest. Measured after the split, deck litness runs 0.52 / 0.56 / 0.76 low-to-high, so the high deck is now the brightest. THE HOUR IS MEASURED: cloud_deck_varieties.json pins sun_elevation at -2.4417 at 20.86 h and the deck windows run ~20.74-20.94, about twelve game minutes — so this hands over at 20.70, just before the window, rather than spending it on the loading screen.
